label: copy phase: fed-back b late in the sequence, esp. when next output is m/h/0/1/b/x/z
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never during the original phase or on <DEL>. It is an input-b detector: 95% of activation mass falls on steps where the fed-back input is b (rate 5%, 29x lift), with a little on h/m inputs. It never fires on the first occurrence of a token. Rate rises sharply with position: almost nothing before recall_idx 3, and the rate climbs from recall_idx 4 to 8 (t>=12 holds most of the mass). It also depends on the token being output (the one that followed b in the original): the strongest activations are b->m (top examples are almost all b m), then h, 0, 1, b, x, z. b followed by p/n/u/j/o/3 is usually silent. Input b with recall_idx>=4 gets 0.92 mass recall but only 0.23 precision. Adding the output-token set gives F1 about 0.56 on dev, so precision stays incomplete.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: b, h, m, 1, 0, -; least: z, o, 3, s) and the token being output (most: m, h, 1, b, 0, x; least: r, c, 2, o); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=6, recall_idx=5, t=15.
